mahjongcraft.guide.crafting.intro: To play, place a Mahjong Table, load a Tile Set into it, and right-click the table. Stools are for sitting around it; loose tiles, sticks and dice are for decoration.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_table: 3 lime or green carpet across the top, a wooden fence in the middle, a wooden slab at the bottom.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_tile_s: 8 Mahjong Tiles around a chest. Right-click a table with it to load it.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_stool: 2 gray carpet on top of 2 sticks.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_book: A book and a Mahjong Tile (shapeless).
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_tile: 6 white concrete beside 3 lime or green concrete. Makes 16.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.mahjong_scorin: Red or black dye above 3 white concrete. Makes 6.
mahjongcraft.guide.recipe.dice: White concrete, red dye and black dye (shapeless). Makes 2.
mahjongcraft.guide.controls.intro: While seated, your hand is shown at the bottom of the screen and the actions you can take appear above it.
mahjongcraft.guide.controls.rebind: The mouse wheel also chooses tiles. Change any key under Options > Controls > Key Binds > MahjongCraft.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.start.title: Starting a game
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.start: Right-click a table with a Tile Set loaded. Friends join the same way, or the host adds bots. Everyone clicks Ready and the host clicks Start.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.goal.title: The goal
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.goal: Make a hand of 14 tiles: four sets (three in a row of one suit, or three of a kind) and one pair. The hand also needs at least one yaku (a scoring pattern) to win.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.turn.title: A turn
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.turn: Draw a tile, then discard one. Your discards stay in front of you for everyone to see.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.calls.title: Calls
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.calls: You can take another player's discard: Chii (a run, only from the player on your left), Pon (three of a kind) or Kan (four of a kind). Calling opens your hand, which removes some yaku.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.riichi.title: Riichi
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.riichi: With a closed hand one tile from winning (tenpai), you can declare riichi by paying a 1000-point stick. It is a yaku by itself, but your hand is then locked.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.win.title: Winning
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.win: Win with a tile you draw (Tsumo) or with another player's discard (Ron). The table panel shows your waits when you are tenpai.
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.furiten.title: Furiten
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.furiten: If you discarded one of your own waiting tiles, you cannot win by Ron, only by Tsumo.
mahjongcraft.guide.yaku.intro: Every winning hand needs at least one yaku. More yaku and dora mean more han, and more han means more points. The Yaku Overview lists every yaku with how many han it is worth.
mahjongcraft.guide.stats.command: Stats are kept per world. See anyone's with /mahjong stats <player>.
mahjongcraft.stats.title: %s's mahjong record
mahjongcraft.stats.unknown_player: No mahjong record for %s in this world
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.sanma.title: 3-player (Sanma)
mahjongcraft.guide.rules.sanma: Set Players to 3 in Edit Rules. The 2m–8m tiles are left out, there is no Chii, and you start with 35,000 points. Set a North aside with the Kita key: it counts as a dora and you draw a replacement tile. A Tsumo is paid only by the two other players.
